Not checked: whether 59a4887 was pushed before the run (the brief does not ask).

B.evidence: The result's 'pins' hold 61 path entries (the brief says 60): 59 carry a registered expected sha256 and 2 are recorded only (the git-excluded evaluate_xm3600_predictions.py, dc00c456, and PD-23.txt, 3c719a6b; no committed pin, as the design's R5 discloses). Re-checked from the sources, not from the script: all 61 recorded sha256 equal the file's sha256 now; the 5 tracked files equal their HEAD blobs; g2b_score.json equals its .sha256 file; scorer_sha256 and prereg_sha256 in g2b_score.json equal the files; the 24 prereg frozen_files (instruments + data) equal their pins; the 23 g2b decodes equal precheck.json runs.*.sha256 (23 of 23); xm3600_full_verdict.json equals selfcheck.json references_sha256; the 6 xm3600 preds equal landed_result_files. Mismatches: []. all_cells_ok True (the registered cells reproduce).

C.evidence: Re-ran 'run' once at HEAD 59a4887 (HEAD unchanged after), 2026-10-20T23:37:28Z to 23:38:33Z, rc 0, python 3.12.3 numpy 2.5.2. Environment as main: env -i HOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin LANG=C.UTF-8, OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL_NUM_THREADS=2, nice -n 15, python3 -E -P -B (plus PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1). The script hard-codes its output path, so I copied the result to <verifier scratch>, removed it from data/results/scar/ (the script refuses otherwise), ran in place, moved the new output to <verifier scratch> and copied the original back with cp -p. Output sha256 242fc04ed80893307aaf93350bb885864d66ea06c9531691da642bcc3e2f6c0b == main's; byte compare (cmp): identical (215731 bytes); stdout identical to main's run.stdout line; stderr byte-identical to main's run.stderr. The output has no time field, so a separate canonical-JSON comparison adds nothing beyond byte identity. After the restore: scar_null_result.json sha256 242fc04e, git status --porcelain identical before and after (174 lines), HEAD unchanged; only the mtime of the data/results/scar/ directory changed.

D.evidence: R and seed: 1000 and 0 re-read from PD-23.txt equal the result's R and seed; the percentile constants 2.5 and 97.5 are the prereg design_constants and equal the result's null_percentiles; each cell holds 1000 finite null_slopes. Summaries: for all 8 cells I recomputed null_mean (tol 1e-12), null_lo/null_hi (own linear-interpolation code, tol 1e-9) and share_same_sign (sign of null slope equals sign of observed slope) from the stored null_slopes: all 8 match (the brief asked for 2). Draws: I replayed one numpy default_rng(0) stream with my own loop (one rng.permutation per image per replicate, images in registered id order, cells in the order cv295, uv231, xm600, s75, each refs1_randk then refs_all), kept the first k_i^(s) classes of each permutation with k_i^(s) = |G_L,i^(s) intersect G_complete,i| from the registered subsets (20 for refs1_randk, 1 for refs_all), shared the gold over the ladder systems, and scored with score_g2b.scores/stat_slope. The stored null_slopes agree exactly (==) at cv295/refs1_randk replicates 0, 1, 999; cv295/refs_all 0, 1; uv231/refs_all 0; s75/refs1_randk 0, 999 (8 replicates in 4 cells; the later cells fix the stream position, so the order set -> level -> replicate -> image holds across cell boundaries). k_i <= |G_complete,i| in every image of every cell. n_images, sum_complete_scored and sum_k_scored_mean_over_subsets recompute for all 8 cells. Image order is integer-sorted for cv295/uv231 and string-sorted for xm600/s75. Limits: the replay reuses score_g2b and the dataset loaders (as the design requires), so it does not re-derive the registered golds; the gate's reproduction of the committed slopes covers them. I did not replay all 8000 replicates.
